svg.title: DockClock architecture: one load in ten steps
svg.desc: 1 The driver's phone sends taps, pins and a bill-of-lading photo over WhatsApp, or RCS as a fallback. 2 AWS End User Messaging Social carries WhatsApp and AWS End User Messaging carries RCS. 3 An AWS Step Functions workflow runs the load; the dock clock stops at the Released tap and a pin within 10 minutes confirms it. 4 Claude on Amazon Bedrock reads the bill-of-lading photo and only raises or lowers confidence. 5 The clause engine, in plain code, sets the verdict and the amount, and the evidence pack is signed with AWS KMS and stored under S3 Object Lock. 6 The dispatcher approves with one WhatsApp tap. 7 A Bedrock AgentCore Harness agent drafts the claim's opening line. 8 Its tool calls pass the AgentCore Gateway and a Cedar policy, and the claim tool refuses unless the amount and digest match the sealed pack. 9 Amazon SES sends the notice, then the claim with a PDF summary and the signed pack. 10 The fictional broker or shipper inbox receives it. A judge console on Amazon CloudFront calls a read-only API that hides typed text and photos on demo loads.
svg.text: One load, from the driver's tap at the dock to the claim in the broker's inbox. Follow the numbers.

g.text: It never sets a time, a verdict or an amount.
Plain code, a Cedar policy and one person's tap.
pins, notice, BOL photo, seal, approval
clock stops at the Released tap
no typed text or photo shown
Amazon SNS / Amazon SQS + dead-letter queue / AWS Lambda
Amazon DynamoDB / EventBridge Scheduler / AWS Secrets Manager
Amazon CloudWatch / AWS X-Ray / AWS CDK
Code, Cedar or a person decides
